title: Spain's Budget Defeat Exposes Governing Fragility · 25 Aug
keywords: Spain, budget paralysis, Pedro Sánchez, coalition government, Spanish parliament, eurozone, inflation, economic growth, services sector, manufacturing, fiscal policy, EU, spending framework
notes: Spain's lower house has rejected the government's 2027 spending framework by a clear margin, delivering a significant legislative blow to Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's coalition and raising doubts about its ability to pass a full state budget. The defeat comes as Spain's economy shows genuine momentum, with services activity at a 40-month high and growth forecasts revised upward, yet inflation running well above the euro area average continues to squeeze ordinary households. The two developments together capture a deepening fault line in one of the eurozone's largest economies: strong macro numbers, fragile political arithmetic.
